semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: 'Database engineering' involves the design, implementation, and maintenance of database systems, which are the infrastructures built to manage data. Therefore, these two domains are essentially covering the same area of expertise and can be considered semantically equivalent.

parent_domains.justification: Database engineering falls under the broader domain of data management since it deals with the development of databases that manage data effectively.
Since creating databases is an aspect of software development, 'database engineering' also fits under the larger umbrella of software engineering.

closest_parent_domain.justification: While database engineering can be seen as part of software engineering, it is more closely associated with data management since its main focus is on handling and organizing data.

child_domains.justification: This is a more specific field within database engineering, focusing on translating natural language to SQL queries, which are used to interact with databases.
As with text-to-sql semantic parsing, this field deals with interaction methods for databases, making it a more specialized aspect of database engineering.

closest_child_domain.justification: 'Text-to-sql semantic parsing' represents a more precise method of converting text inputs into SQL queries, directly related to how databases are queried and interacted with in the realm of database engineering.

sibling_domains.justification: Within the parent domain of data management, data strategy involves planning how data will be handled and utilized, similar to how database engineering focuses on structuring and managing data storage.
This involves techniques applied before actual data processing, just as database engineering involves setting up the infrastructure beforehand.
Similar to database engineering, which involves organizing data in databases, data curation involves maintaining and managing data using various methods.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: 'Data strategy' is closely tied to database engineering as both involve higher-level planning and organization of data handling and management, aligning with the goal of efficient and effective data use.

unrelated_domains.justification: This domain is focused on handling specific types of data pertaining to patients, which is a separate application area and not focused on the database technology itself.
Relational reasoning deals with the logic and relationships between data rather than the technical aspects of storing and accessing it.
This is concerned with the design and analysis of algorithms, which are independent of the database-specific tasks.
While it involves optimizing systems, it does not specifically pertain to databases.
This specialization of software engineering focuses more on the integration and development for machine learning purposes, which often doesn't directly involve database tasks.
This pertains to the analysis of software systems, rather than the engineering of databases specifically.
While related to data, this domain focuses on ensuring accuracy and reliability rather than the storage and management solutions offered by database engineering.
Data analysis concerns analyzing data, not the creation and management of the systems that store data.
This refers to abstracting and representing concepts, often used within software development but not directly related to building and maintaining databases.
This refers to optimizing the use of data, which is an outcome but not directly tied to the engineering of databases.
Preprocessing involves preparing data for analysis but is not focused on the structural or engineering aspects of databases.
